examples.en: I felt sympathy after hearing that story.
I helped him out of sympathy.

examples.ko: 아이들은 길 잃은 강아지에게 동정심을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The children felt pity for the lost puppy.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 보면 동정심 많은 사람들이 기부를 해요.
examples.en: On the news, compassionate people make donations.
Sympathy alone can't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 나는 그 사람에게 동정심이 하나도 안 들어요.
examples.en: I don't feel any sympathy for that person.

explain: '동정심이 생기다/들다', '동정심을 느끼다'처럼 써요. 불쌍하게 여기는 마음이라서 상대가 자기를 낮춰 본다고 느낄 수 있어서 '동정하지 마세요'라고 싫어하는 사람도 있어요. 더 깊고 따뜻한 마음은 '연민'이라고 하고, 글에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: You say '동정심이 생기다/들다' or '동정심을 느끼다'. Because it means feeling sorry for someone, the other person may feel looked down on, and some people say '동정하지 마세요' (don't pity me). '연민' is a deeper, warmer feeling and is used more in writing.

examples.ko: 지난 몇 달 동안 마음고생이 심했어요.
examples.en: The past few months have been emotionally very hard.
You look like you've been through a lot emotionally.
After all the emotional hardship, a good result came out.
My parents suffered a lot of worry because of the child.
You've been through a lot all this time. Thank you so much.
I lost a lot of weight because of the emotional stress.

explain: 몸이 힘든 것이 아니라 걱정이나 눈치 때문에 마음이 힘든 걸 말해요. '마음고생(을) 하다', '마음고생이 심하다'로 쓰고, 위로할 때 '마음고생 많았어요'라고 해요. 몸이 힘든 '몸고생'과 같이 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to hardship felt in the heart because of worry or having to watch others' reactions, not physical hardship. It is used as '마음고생(을) 하다' or '마음고생이 심하다', and to comfort someone you say '마음고생 많았어요'. It is sometimes paired with '몸고생', physical hardship.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀에서는 지각이 큰 문젯거리예요.
examples.en: These days, being late is a big problem on our team.

examples.ko: 이 정도는 문젯거리도 아니니까 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: This much isn't even a problem, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 반에서 문젯거리로 불려서 속상해해요.
examples.en: That kid is upset about being called a troublemaker in class.

examples.ko: 이 낡은 차는 요즘 문젯거리만 만들어요.
examples.en: This old car does nothing but cause trouble these days.

examples.ko: 주차 문제가 이웃 사이에서 문젯거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: The parking issue has become a problem among the neighbors.

examples.ko: 제가 또 문젯거리를 만든 것 같아서 미안해요.
examples.en: I'm sorry, it seems I've created trouble again.

explain: '골칫거리'와 비슷하게 쓰지만, '골칫거리'는 머리가 아픈 느낌이 더 강해요. '문젯거리'는 문제가 되는 일이나 사람을 가리켜요. 사람에게 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used like '골칫거리', but '골칫거리' feels more like a headache. '문젯거리' points to the thing or person causing the problem. Used about a person, it can sound insulting.

examples.en: After the exams, a study slump hit me.
Every athlete goes through a slump.
I went on a trip to get out of my slump.
I'm in a slump lately and don't feel like doing anything.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 긴 슬럼프 끝에 새 앨범을 냈어요.
examples.en: That singer released a new album after a long slump.
A friend helped me when I fell into a slump.

explain: 운동, 공부, 일이 한동안 잘 안 되는 시기에 써요. 그냥 기분이 안 좋은 건 '우울하다'이고, 슬럼프는 성과가 떨어질 때 말해요. '슬럼프가 오다', '슬럼프에 빠지다', '슬럼프를 극복하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: It is for a period when sports, study, or work stops going well for a while. Just feeling down is '우울하다'; 슬럼프 is used when your results drop. It pairs with fixed verbs: '슬럼프가 오다' (a slump comes), '슬럼프에 빠지다' (fall into a slump), '슬럼프를 극복하다' (overcome a slump).

examples.en: The main cause of this accident was drowsy driving.

examples.ko: 이 병의 주원인을 아직 찾지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't found the main cause of this illness yet.
Oversleeping is the main reason I'm late.
Experts point to lack of sleep as the main cause.
Let's first find out what the main cause is.
The investigation into the main cause of the fire is over.

explain: 여러 원인 중 가장 중요한 원인을 말해요. 일상에서는 '이유'라고 많이 하고, '주원인'은 사고·병·문제를 설명하는 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the most important cause among several. In daily talk people say '이유' more, while '주원인' often appears in news and reports that explain accidents, illnesses or problems.

examples.en: This film is rated as a good work.
My ability was assessed by the test score.
That player is regarded as the best.
I was upset because I wasn't judged fairly.
It's a highly rated book, so give it a read.
It may be reassessed later.

explain: '좋다', '나쁘다'처럼 다른 사람에게 점수나 가치가 매겨진다는 말이에요. 'A로 평가되다'의 틀이 많아요. 내가 직접 평가하면 '평가하다'를 쓰고, 칭찬이면 '높이 평가하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a person or thing is given a value or score by others. It is often used in the pattern 'is rated as A'. When you judge something yourself, the active verb is used, and for praise people say they rate something highly.
